task.description: WF-02 Step 2b (Review) for REQ-039 at commit cacb694 on feature/WF02-REQ-039. Reviewed the full diff master...HEAD against the approved design (docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md, post-rework), the issue #71 requirement text (all 9 ACs), decisions 0004/0005/0006, anti-patterns.md, and reviewer.md's apps/bot-specific checks. Independently assessed BACKEND-DEV's two flagged issues rather than trusting either self-report.

result.summary:
PASS. Checks actually performed, not asserted:

1. DOMAIN LOGIC PLACEMENT (decisions/0004): all decision logic -- the returning-guest branch, the field-collection carrier parse/format functions, getCompanionDisplayData's phone/email-excluding SELECT, the redeemInviteCode extension (companionProfile param, invitedByUserId write, guarded Profile insert) -- lives in domain/inviteCode.ts and domain/profile.ts. handlers/companion.ts and the new branch in handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink only sequence replies and call domain functions; no admission/capacity/attribution rule is embedded in a handler body. Confirmed by reading the full diffs of both handler files and inviteCode.ts, not by taking BACKEND-DEV's account on trust.

2. NO now()/current_timestamp IN A TIME-DEPENDENT PREDICATE (decisions/0006): grepped inviteCode.ts, companion.ts, start.ts for now()/current_timestamp/sql`now -- none found. evaluationTime (new Date()) is passed as an explicit parameter into redeemInviteCode from both call sites (handlers/companion.ts's confirm callback, handlers/start.ts's direct-redemption branch), matching the existing REQ-038 discipline. writeAuditLog's `at` uses the same passed-in evaluationTime, not a DB default.

3. MIGRATIONS/SCHEMA (decisions/0005, AC2): `git status apps/bot/drizzle` clean, `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` empty, `git grep -n companion apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` returns exactly the pre-existing grantsCompanionOf column. No migration to review as SQL; no SECURITY-REVIEWER sign-off needed under S13 since nothing is dropped/rewritten.

4. ISSUE 1 (host notification fires from both the confirm-callback path and the returning-guest direct-redemption path) -- CONFIRMED CORRECT, not a defect. Traced both call sites: handlers/companion.ts's makeCompanionConfirmCallbackHandler reaches the reduced-field conversation only when handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink found existingProfile === null (§2) and routed to the field-collection prompt instead of redeeming directly. A returning guest (existingProfile !== null) never enters the field-collection flow or reaches the confirm callback at all -- the two call sites are mutually exclusive for a single guest's single redemption attempt, so there is no scenario where both fire for the same registration. This is backstopped structurally regardless: sendLedgeredNotification's (registrationId, kind) unique-index idempotency (unchanged mechanism, §0 table of the design) makes a double-send for the same registration impossible even under a hypothetical race. AC7's 'holds identically for a returning guest' gap in the design's own §7 AC-map (BACKEND-DEV's flagged interpretive completion) is a reasonable, correctly-scoped reading of AC7's own text ('Both the guest and the host receive exactly one message on a successful companion registration' states no returning-guest carve-out) -- not a business-rule invention. Confirmed correct.

5. ISSUE 2 (typed /redeem was never in this design's scope for companion codes) -- CONFIRMED NOT A GAP; correctly out of scope for REQ-039 as written, not a defect requiring rework. Read issue #71's full text: the requirement's own description narrates only the link-forwarding entry point ('A host holding a COMPANION code... FORWARDS THE LINK to their guest. The guest opens it and redeems...') and never mentions /redeem for companion codes anywhere. This is a meaningful textual contrast with REQ-038 (issue #70), whose own description explicitly says 'REDEMPTION BY BOTH ROUTES' and whose own AC1 explicitly requires verification 'BOTH via ?start=i_<code> and by typing the code' -- REQ-039 has no equivalent 'both routes' language anywhere, and none of its 9 ACs specifies a /redeem verification path (each AC's stated verification method names only the link/consent/field-collection flow). The approved, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-gated design (docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md) independently reached the same reading: its own §0 table and artifacts_in list name only handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink as the modified handler, with handlers/registration.ts (the /redeem command) never listed as in scope. I traced the actual behavior to confirm the gap is real but narrow: makeRedeemCommandHandler (handlers/registration.ts) only reaches redeemInviteCode directly, bypassing resolveInviteDeepLink entirely, when flowUser.consentPdAt is already set at call time; if not yet consented, its own consent prompt resumes via handlers/start.ts's consent callback -> resolveInviteDeepLink, which DOES apply this requirement's companion branch. So the uncovered case is narrow: an already-consented user (per REQ-019, typically already holds a Profile row from write-as-you-go onboarding, in which case they'd be treated as a 'returning guest' under this design's own Open Question 1 resolution anyway -- attribution still applies, just no field-collection or host notification, which is the SAME behavior a returning guest gets via the deep-link route) typing /redeem with a companion code they obtained by some other means. BACKEND-DEV filed this as an unresolved DESIGN GAP for ORCH/CODE-DESIGNER rather than silently inventing scope or silently leaving it undocumented -- correct handling per core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything scope boundary and No Issue Left Local-Only. ORCH should log this as its own issue (candidate title: '/redeem entry point untested/unspecified for companion codes') rather than block this gate on it, since the approved design and the requirement's own text both scope this out.

6. RETURNING-GUEST FIX: confirmed getProfileByUserId(db, userId) is checked in start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink before branching (only evaluated when isCompanionCode is true, per design §2's 'zero behavior change' instruction for non-companion codes). Confirmed the guarded insert -- createWalkinProfile's new onConflictDoNothing({ target: profiles.userId }) option, only passed true at the companion call site in inviteCode.ts, REQ-030's own call site in domain/walkin.ts unchanged (verified via diff, byte-for-byte). Confirmed invitedByUserId: codeRow.grantsCompanionOf is written unconditionally on both the insert and the existingRegistrationId update branch (inviteCode.ts lines ~800-825), independent of companionProfile -- a no-op for personal/bulk codes since their grantsCompanionOf is always null.

7. S1 CONSENT-BEFORE-STORAGE: traced resolveInviteDeepLink -- the `if (!hasConsented)` early-return (unchanged position) runs before any lookup; codeRow/existingProfile reads happen only after hasConsented is true; the field-collection branch (isCompanionCode && existingProfile === null) only sends a reply (ctx.reply), no DB call. handlers/companion.ts's makeCompanionTextReplyHandler (re-prompt on parse failure) and the confirm message render also perform zero DB writes -- the single write is inside redeemInviteCode, reached only from the confirm-tap callback. Nothing (User edit beyond the pre-existing bare-row /start creates, Profile row, partial draft) is written before the single confirm+write tap for a brand-new guest.

8. S3/S11: getCompanionDisplayData's SELECT clause (inviteCode.ts) lists firstName/lastName/tgUsername/company only -- profiles.phone and profiles.email are never in the query, so they structurally cannot appear in the composed host-notification text. Grepped for phone/log/audit interaction: the writeAuditLog call inside redeemInviteCode's registration write (inviteCode.ts ~line 863) has payload: { eventId, inviteCodeId } only -- unchanged from before this requirement, never carried a profile field. No console/log call anywhere in the diff references companionProfile.phone or parsed fields' phone value.

9. REQ-038 NON-REGRESSION: `git diff master...HEAD --stat -- '*.test.ts'` returns empty -- zero test files touched anywhere in this diff, confirming BACKEND-DEV's claim that companionProfile defaulting to null and sender defaulting to null required no edits to REQ-038's own test suite.

10. start.ts's sender param: makeStartHandler/makeConsentCallbackHandler both gained sender: NotificationSender | null = null as a trailing optional parameter; production wiring (index.ts) passes notificationSender, existing test construction (makeStartHandler(db)) is unaffected by the default. Confirmed via diff and the passing test run.

11. NO NEW NPM WORKSPACE / no change to build output shape -- diff stat shows no apps/* package.json, no Dockerfile change; the docker-build gate in reviewer.md's step 7 does not apply here.

12. LINT/BUILD/TESTS re-run independently: `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -- clean. `npm run build -w apps/bot` (tsc) -- clean. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from apps/bot -- 88 test files, 810 tests, all passed, single run, no ISS-0031 contention pattern observed (no failures to require a second run).

13. ANTI-PATTERNS: no entry in docs/agents/anti-patterns.md applies to this diff.

Scope: matches issue #71's 9 ACs; no unrelated changes bundled in (diff stat confined to the companion flow's own files, i18n additions, and the standard handoff/registry bookkeeping).
issues: Not a blocking finding for this gate, but should be logged as its own tracked issue per ISSUE_QUEUE.md: the typed /redeem command path for a companion code (an already-consented user with no existing Profile row typing /redeem <event_id> <companion_code> directly) bypasses the reduced-field collection flow and the host notification (falls through to companionProfile: null, the same path a returning guest takes). Confirmed this is legitimately out of REQ-039's own written scope (see result.summary point 5) rather than a defect in this implementation -- filed here as a MINOR handoff note, not a rework item, per BACKEND-DEV's own correct flagging. ORCH should allocate an issue id and decide whether a follow-up requirement is warranted.

next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory for apps/bot/** changes, and especially warranted here given S1's stakes (consent-before-storage) and the new companion_registered notification's S3/S11 scope.
